newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds open stronger on tame U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds open stronger on tame U.S. data.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened stronger on Thursday, as tame U.S. gross domestic product data for the second quarter helped send prices higher in both countries, analysts said.

"It was the excellent U.S. numbers," said Joe Lee, a portfolio manager with Laketon Investment Management. "It's the continuous reasonable good growth in the economy with very little evidence of inflation being a major factor."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.31 to C$122.64 to yield 6.305 percent, a record low yield for the 30-year benchmark.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 13/32 to yield 6.30 percent. The spread between the bonds moved to one basis point from a negative spread of one basis point at Monday's close.
Bonds in both countries rallied after the U.S. Commerce Department on Thursday said GDP grew at a 2.2 percent annual rate in the second quarter, down from a revised 4.9 percent in the first quarter.
Analysts said the downward revision, as well as the tame implicit price deflator portion of the report, were bullish for fixed-income markets in both countries.
In new issue news, the Government of Canada said it planned to auction on August 6 C$2.3 billion of bonds with an unspecified coupon maturing on June 1, 2008.

The Bank of Canada will buy at least C$345 million of the new bonds. The bonds, which will be dated and delivered on August 15, pay interest on June 1 and December 1, the government said. No bonds mature on August 15, 1997.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.08 to C$110.78 to yield 5.793 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond fell 1/32 to yield 6.05 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds widened to 26 basis points from 23 basis points at Wednesday's close.
